subtitle: Trade, Fire and the Birth of a Sea War

panels.shot: epic wide of a stormy Calicut harbor, one Portuguese ship firing while another Indian vessel burns in the distance
panels.action: Vasco da Gama stands at a ship’s rail, face hard, watching a distant pilgrim ship engulfed in flames near the Malabar coast as cannon smoke drifts over a tense harbor.

dialogue.text: In 1500–1502, Pedro Álvares Cabral and Vasco da Gama turned Calicut’s trading coast into a battlefield, where a factory riot and a burning pilgrim ship began a brutal war for the Indian Ocean.

i18n.hi: १५००–१५०२ में पेद्रो आल्वारेश कब्राल और वास्को दा गामा ने कोझिकोड का कारोबार तट जंग का मैदान बना दिया, जहाँ फैक्ट्री दंगा और ज़ायरीन जहाज़ की आग से हिंद महासागर की खूनी जंग शुरू हुई।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a map table in a dim cabin, Indian Ocean routes marked in ink
panels.action: Pedro Álvares Cabral bends over a nautical chart lit by lamplight, the coast of Malabar circled, Lisbon’s royal seal heavy on the table beside a rosary and a pepper sample.

dialogue.text: After Vasco da Gama’s first voyage, the Portuguese Crown sent Pedro Álvares Cabral in 1500 to make Calicut a gateway to a spice monopoly, backed not just by gold, but by guns.

i18n.hi: वास्को दा गामा की पहली यात्रा के बाद, पुर्तगाली ताज ने १५०० में पेद्रो आल्वारेश कब्राल को भेजा, ताकि कोझिकोड को मसाला मोनोपॉली का दरवाज़ा बना सके—सोने से नहीं, तोपों से भी।

panels.shot: wide harbor view as Cabral’s fleet anchors off Calicut, bustling local craft around
panels.action: Cabral, cloaked and rigid, stands on the deck of his flagship as sleek Malabari dhows weave through the waves, coconut palms and the warehouses of Calicut lining the shore beyond.

dialogue.text: Calicut, ruled by the Zamorin, was a free port where Arab, Indian and other merchants shared the pepper trade. The Portuguese wanted privileged access, lower prices and tighter control.

i18n.hi: ज़मोरिन के राज वाला कोझिकोड खुला बंदरगाह था, जहाँ अरब, हिंदुस्तानी और दूसरे सौदागर काली मिर्च का व्यापार बाँटते थे। पुर्तगालीों को ख़ास रियायतें, सस्ते दाम और सख़्त कंट्रोल चाहिए था।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a newly established factory, bales of pepper stacked, tense faces
panels.action: Cabral stands stiffly in the Portuguese factory, flanked by armed guards, facing a group of local merchants in simple cotton robes, their brows furrowed as clerks weigh pepper on brass scales.

dialogue.text: A factory was set up in Calicut. But disputes over prices, customs dues and rival merchants quickly sharpened. Each side accused the other of cheating, each felt the other was arrogant.

i18n.hi: कोझिकोड में एक फैक्ट्री खड़ी हुई। पर दाम, चुंगी और टक्कर वाले सौदागरों पर झगड़े तुरंत तेज़ हो गए। दोनों तरफ से एक-दूसरे पर चोरी के इलज़ाम, दोनों को लगा सामने वाला घमंडी है।

panels.shot: tight, tense interior with shouting figures, Portuguese guards gripping weapons
panels.action: Within the dim factory hall, local traders surge forward angrily while Portuguese soldiers clutch their swords, Cabral in the background raising a hand in alarm as confusion spills into violence.

dialogue.text: Portuguese accounts describe an attack on the factory after these quarrels escalated, with many of their men killed. The details are murky, but the break with Calicut was sudden and bloody.

i18n.hi: पुर्तगाली बयान बताते हैं कि झगड़े बढ़ने पर फैक्ट्री पर हमला हुआ, उनके कई आदमी मारे गए। तमाम बातें धुंधली हैं, पर कोझिकोड से रिश्ता अचानक और खून-खराबे में टूटा।

panels.shot: low-angle view from the shore as Cabral’s ships unleash cannon fire toward Calicut
panels.action: Cabral, jaw set, signals from his quarterdeck as cannons roar, Portuguese ships lined in formation hurl stone shot toward the waterfront buildings of Calicut under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: Cabral answered with bombardment. Portuguese sources say his ships shelled Calicut’s shore and seized or burned Indian vessels, turning a trade quarrel into open, punitive war.

i18n.hi: कब्राल ने तोपों से जवाब दिया। पुर्तगाली सूत्रों के मुताबिक उसके जहाज़ों ने कोझिकोड के किनारे पर गोले बरसाए और हिंदुस्तानी जहाज़ों को पकड़ा या जला दिया—एक कारोबारी झगड़ा खुली सज़ाई जंग बना दिया।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over the sea as mixed Indian shipping scatters from Portuguese warships
panels.action: From high above, small merchant ships scatter across the glittering water as Cabral’s larger caravels cut through the waves, smoke traces marking where masts and hulls burn offshore.

dialogue.text: Ships belonging to Calicut-linked traders were targeted. The message was clear: resistance to Portuguese demands could be met not with negotiation, but with destruction at sea.

i18n.hi: कोझिकोड से जुड़े सौदागरों के जहाज़ निशाने पर थे। संदेश साफ था: पुर्तगाली मांगों का विरोध अब बात-चीत से नहीं, समुंदर पर तबाही से मिलेगा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Cabral meeting Cochin’s ruler in a coastal courtyard
panels.action: Cabral, in ornate armor, kneels slightly before the ruler of Cochin under a palm-fringed canopy, with scribes and guards watching as chests of gifts lie open between them.

dialogue.text: After breaking with Calicut, Cabral moved toward Cochin and other rival ports. Portuguese sources describe new alliances there, binding their guns to local enemies of the Zamorin’s city.

i18n.hi: कोझिकोड से नाता तोड़कर कब्राल कोच्चि और दूसरे टक्कर के बंदरगाहों की तरफ बढ़ा। पुर्तगाली रिकॉर्ड नई सांठगांठों की बात करते हैं, जहाँ उनकी तोपें ज़मोरिन के दुश्मन शहरों से जा मिलीं।

panels.shot: transition shot: parchment letter bearing the royal Portuguese seal being signed
panels.action: In a candlelit Lisbon chamber, a royal hand signs orders as Vasco da Gama stands nearby, the seal pressed onto a letter that mentions Malabar, spices, and punishment for those resisting.

dialogue.text: Lisbon watched. Cabral’s clash with Calicut hardened attitudes. By the time Vasco da Gama sailed again in 1502, Portuguese policy mixed commerce, crusading language and deliberate terror.

i18n.hi: लिस्बन सब देख रहा था। कब्राल की टक्कर ने कोझिकोड पर नज़रें कड़ी कर दीं। १५०२ में जब वास्को दा गामा फिर निकला, पुर्तगाली चाल में कारोबार, धर्मयुद्ध की ज़बान और सोची-समझी दहशत घुल चुकी थी।

panels.shot: wide ocean shot as da Gama’s fleet meets the large pilgrim ship Miri
panels.action: On the open Arabian Sea, da Gama’s armed fleet draws alongside the massive, high-sided Miri, its decks crowded with people, its hull richly painted as waves roll beneath both ships.

dialogue.text: In 1502, Gaspar Correia’s account says, da Gama encountered the Miri, a great ship carrying Muslim pilgrims and valuable cargo, bound from India toward the Red Sea and beyond.

i18n.hi: १५०२ में, गास्पार कोरेया के हिसाब से, दा गामा की मुलाकात ‘मिरी’ से हुई—एक बड़ा जहाज़, जिसमें मुस्लिम ज़ायरीन और कीमती माल था, भारत से लाल सागर और आगे की तरफ जा रहा था।

panels.shot: medium shot across the water: da Gama shouting from his deck toward the Miri
panels.action: Da Gama stands at the rail of his flagship, arm extended toward the Miri, his officers behind him, while figures on the pilgrim ship gesture anxiously and raise their hands in appeal.

dialogue.speaker: pedro_alvares_cabral_and_vasco_da_gama
dialogue.text: The king’s justice reaches these seas. You will pay, or be an example.

i18n.hi: राजा का न्याय इन समंदरों तक आता है। चुकाओगे, नहीं तो मिसाल बनोगे।

panels.shot: closer shot of the Miri’s deck with kneeling figures and chests of goods displayed
panels.action: On the crowded deck of the Miri, merchants and pilgrims kneel with outstretched hands beside opened chests of textiles and spices, children clinging to elders as the sea heaves gently.

dialogue.text: Correia’s narrative describes ransom talks and pleas for mercy. The ship’s people offered goods and wealth, hoping to buy safety for their vessel and those crowded upon it.

i18n.hi: कोरेया की कहानी में फिरौती की बातें और रहम की गुहार हैं। जहाज़ वालों ने माल-दौलत पेश की, ताकि जहाज़ और उस पर ठुसे हुए लोगों की जान बच सके।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle from the Miri’s deck, ropes and flames beginning along her side
panels.action: Seen from the Miri’s deck, Portuguese sailors on boats lash it with ropes while small fires flicker along the hull, smoke beginning to curl as sky and sea remain deceptively calm.

dialogue.text: Portuguese sources, including Correia, say that when these negotiations failed, da Gama had the Miri seized and set alight, using it as a public act of terror on the open sea.

i18n.hi: पुर्तगाली बयान, जिनमें कोरेया भी है, कहते हैं कि बात-चीत टूटते ही दा गामा ने मिरी को कब्ज़े में लेकर आग लगा दी—खुले समुंदर में इसे खुली दहशत का तमाशा बना दिया।

panels.shot: wide, distant shot of the Miri burning, other ships watching from afar
panels.action: From far off, da Gama’s fleet lies in a loose ring while the Miri burns at the center, towering flames rising from its decks as silhouettes of onlookers stand silent on Portuguese ships.

dialogue.text: Correia’s account speaks of hundreds aboard—perhaps two to four hundred—trapped on the burning pilgrim ship. The numbers differ in sources, but all agree the human loss was immense.

i18n.hi: कोरेया के हिसाब में सैकड़ों लोग—शायद दो से चार सौ—उस जलती ज़ायरीन जहाज़ पर फँसे थे। गिनती स्रोतों में बदलती है, पर सब मानते हैं कि इंसानी नुक़सान बेहिसाब था।

panels.shot: close-up on da Gama’s face lit by firelight reflection, expression cold and resolved
panels.action: Da Gama watches from his deck, the reflection of distant flames dancing in his eyes, his expression unreadable as the crackling glow paints his armor with an orange sheen.

dialogue.text: Modern historians note that religious language sharpened da Gama’s actions, but behind it lay a goal: to frighten Muslim and Indian merchants, and reshape Indian Ocean trade by force.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक इतिहासकार कहते हैं कि धार्मिक ज़बान ने दा गामा की करतूतों को नुकीला बनाया, पर पीछे असल मक़सद था: मुस्लिम और हिंदुस्तानी सौदागरों को डराना, और हिंद महासागर का व्यापार ज़बरदस्ती मोड़ना।

panels.shot: shoreline shot back at Calicut, angry crowds and mariners gesturing to the sea
panels.action: On Calicut’s beach, mariners and townsfolk cluster in agitation, pointing toward the horizon where faint smoke hangs, the Zamorin’s officials listening grimly to heated complaints.

dialogue.text: News of Cabral’s bombardment and da Gama’s burning of the Miri spread. For Calicut’s merchants and rulers, these acts marked the Portuguese as traders who wielded terror, not trust.

i18n.hi: कब्राल की गोलाबारी और दा गामा की मिरी को जलाने की ख़बरें फैल गईं। कोझिकोड के सौदागर और हाकिमों के लिए ये काम पुर्तगालियों को ऐसे सौदागर साबित करते हैं जो भरोसा नहीं, दहशत चलाते हैं।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot: Portuguese ships near Cochin, Calicut’s harbor bristling with local fleets
panels.action: Across a split seascape, Portuguese caravels anchor near Cochin’s protective shore on one side, while on the other, Calicut’s harbor teems with Indian ships arming and preparing for future conflict.

dialogue.text: From this moment, alliances hardened. The Portuguese drew closer to Cochin and other rivals, while Calicut and its seafaring captains began to see the ocean itself as a new front in war.

i18n.hi: यहीं से ढाँचे सख़्त हो गए। पुर्तगाली कोच्चि और दूसरे दुश्मन बंदरगाहों के और करीब जा लगे, जबकि कोझिकोड और उसके समुंदरी कप्तान खुद समंदर को जंग की नई सरहद समझने लगे।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of a Malabari war captain on a deck, Portuguese ship distant
panels.action: A Malabari sea captain stands firm on his deck, hand on the rail, watching a far Portuguese ship under full sail, monsoon clouds gathering over the darkening sea between them.

dialogue.text: In the years ahead, figures like the Kunjali Marakkars would rise from this coast, answering cannon with counter-raids, as trade routes between India and the world turned into contested battle-lines.

i18n.hi: आने वाले बरसों में कुंजाली मरक्कार जैसे नाम इसी तट से उठेंगे, तोप का जवाब छापामार से देंगे, और हिंदुस्तान से दुनिया तक की राहें खुली मंडी से भिड़ंत की लड़ाई-रेखाएँ बन जाएँगी।

panels.shot: final contemplative shot: charred driftwood from a ship on a quiet beach at sunset
panels.action: On a calm evening shore, a piece of blackened ship’s timber lies at the water’s edge, waves gently touching it as the sun sinks, while a lone figure sits far away, staring out to sea.

dialogue.text: Cabral’s ruined factory and the burning of the Miri show how, when commerce chooses terror, every ship becomes a battlefield and every harbor remembers that trust can be lost in a single fire.

i18n.hi: कब्राल की उजड़ी फैक्ट्री और मिरी की जलती हुई शक्ल दिखाती है कि जब कारोबार दहशत चुनता है, तो हर जहाज़ जंग का मैदान बन जाता है और हर बंदरगाह को याद रहता है कि भरोसा एक ही आग में खो सकता है।

title_i18n.en: Cabral's Factory and the Miri Fire
title_i18n.hi: कब्राल की फैक्ट्री और मिरी की आग
